title: Devlog - Grimoire of Hecate : Tower of Starlight
author: NotaDevAI
selftext:
First things first, here’s the game!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/5078840/Grimoire\_of\_Hecate\_\_Tower\_of\_Starlight/

I wanted to share a little about how things have been going since I released the first demo on August 20. I figured there are probably other devs going through something similar.

As of September 18, almost a month later, the game has just under 90,000 impressions on Steam and 70 wishlists. Nothing to brag about, haha.

For the first two weeks after releasing the demo, I tried my hand at marketing for the first time. I posted on Reddit and other online communities, streamed the game on Steam for an hour or two a day during the first few days, put together a press kit, and reached out to creators and media outlets across different languages.

I used quite a lot of AI while making the game, and the visuals aren’t exactly eye-catching yet, so it didn’t get much attention on social media. To be fair, I didn’t post all that much either.

The Steam livestreams had a fairly steady trickle of viewers, peaking at around 10 at once, but nobody said anything in chat. I did usually see two or three new wishlists after each stream. I’m still not sure whether that was thanks to the streams themselves or just the extra visibility from having recently released the demo.

Once the press kit was ready, I emailed around 300 creators and media contacts in total. No creator has posted a gameplay video yet, but one Japanese outlet and one French outlet were kind enough to write articles about the game.

The best thing to come out of all this, though, was the feedback. Even when people couldn’t make a video or write an article, more of them than I expected took the time to really play the game and send me detailed thoughts.

Around 20 people I reached through email and another 10 from Discord communities spent a meaningful amount of time playtesting it. Finding playtesters had been a struggle, so I was honestly really grateful. One person from Japan even played for over five hours and sent me nearly three full pages of feedback.

Now that it’s been almost a month, that initial visibility on Steam has settled down. With me no longer doing regular marketing, I can definitely see fewer new people coming in.

Still, I’ve put marketing aside for now to work through the feedback and get the game into better shape before Steam Next Fest.

Here’s what I’m focusing on:

\- Making the art more consistent and less obviously AI-generated. This has probably been the hardest part. I’ve been using Aseprite to give the graphics a pixel-art look, but the results aren’t quite where I want them yet.

\- Improving the pacing. A lot of the feedback said the rewards were too stingy, which made the game feel slow.

\- Adding rewards to each event.

\- Adding new spells and items.

\- Changing the map’s visual style.

\- Improving combat and making hits feel more satisfying. This one is really difficult too. Making a game that’s actually fun is no easy thing.

I pushed an update to Steam today with some of these changes, but there’s still a long way to go. I’ll probably keep focusing on the game itself until Next Fest, then spend more time on marketing again.
